messages.content: Write a realistic SMS conversation, 4 to 8 short texts, between a patient in rural North Dakota with hypertension or type 2 diabetes and Northline Care's weekly check-in agent. Situation: insurance denied test strips or a claim question.

SMS Conversation #104 — pt-1001 (Type 2 Diabetes, Test Strip Denial)

Patient: "Hi northline my insurance just rejected my test strip refill. I have maybe 10 left. What do I do?"

Agent: "That's frustrating. I can't work with insurance directly, but let's figure this out. Have you called your insurance company to ask why they denied it?"

Patient: "Not yet but I'm worried they'll deny it again. What happens if they say no?"

Agent: "Good question. If they won't budge, I can escalate you to a nurse — they know workarounds. Median response time is about 31 hours. Want me to do that?"

Patient: "Yeah maybe. Been on metformin for 2 years no problems. Just stressed about running out of strips before it's fixed"

Agent: "Got it — logging your metformin. Since you're worried about a gap coming, I'm escalating to a nurse today. They'll reach out within 31 hours and help figure next steps."

Patient: "Should I ration the strips I have left? Like test every other day instead of every day?"

Agent: "Don't change your testing routine without talking to your nurse or doctor — that's a clinical call I can't make. But they'll discuss this with you when they call."

theme: insurance denied test strips or a claim question
